data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism ends with the claim that 'the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.' But the same mechanism identifies corroboration as the selection criterion driving the process. Corroboration is itself a structural property: a theory is corroborated by virtue of its logical content, testability, and having survived severe tests — all features of the theory's internal structure. If the underlying structure of theories is genuinely irrelevant to the outcome, then corroboration — which is defined entirely in terms of structural properties — cannot be the causal mechanism of selection either. The target thus simultaneously makes structure load-bearing (via corroboration) and denies its relevance, producing an internal contradiction that undermines the entire analogy. Unlike prior objections targeting the descriptive/normative gap, this objection shows that even on the target's own purely descriptive-evolutionary terms, the argument is self-defeating: the selection criterion it invokes depends on exactly the kind of structural relation it declares irrelevant.
